I reproduced the failure: two editions with the same ISBN, publication years 1974 and 1975, and similar author names raise `KeyError('db_name')` at threshold 515 after expansion.

The likely fix spans three places: [expand_record](/app/openlibrary/catalog/utils/__init__.py:294) copies authors without generating identifiers; [add_db_name](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:602) is called separately in one matching path; and [existing-edition conversion](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/match.py:52) duplicates the formatting logic. [compare_author_fields](/app/openlibrary/catalog/merge/merge_marc.py:144) then reads `db_name` directly. Centralizing `add_db_name` in catalog utils, calling it during expansion, and passing only name and date fields into existing-edition expansion would cover the reported path, including authors without dates and records with absent, empty, or `None` authors.

The two focused existing tests pass, but both supply identifiers manually. One low-threshold fixture supplies an identifier that differs from its author name, so its expected score may need review when identifiers are generated uniformly. Centralized author identifier generation in catalog utils and made record expansion apply it to every author. Existing-edition conversion now supplies name and birth or death dates for expansion to process. Matching also recognizes equivalent names in natural and catalog order.

The updated tests cover missing identifiers, absent or empty author lists, and the 515 threshold case. The local add_book and merge tests finished with **82 passed, 1 expected failure, and 2 unexpected passes**.
